body.x: DeepFusion AI (CEO Sung Hun Yu) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9, as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.

DeepFusion AI is a startup that has developed AI solutions based on so-called sensor fusion. The company develops software that enables real-time perception of surrounding environments by fusing multiple sensors, including radar, cameras, and LiDAR, and provides technologies that enhance safety and efficiency across fields such as autonomous driving, defense, and maritime applications.

Its core technology is the ‘RAPA (Real-time Attention-based Pillar Architecture)’ engine, which delivers stable perception performance across diverse environments through a radar-centered sensor fusion architecture. According to the company, by differentiating sensor configurations, it has diversified its product lineup, allowing customers to flexibly select and apply options optimized for their specific environments.

At the exhibition, DeepFusion AI plans to once again highlight the differentiation and competitiveness of its proprietary real-time perception technology by introducing the functions and application cases of ‘RAPA-R,’ which was previously selected for a top AI innovation award. Built on a multi-radar architecture, RAPA-R is characterized by outstanding stability and highly accurate perception performance even in complex environments.

By using multiple radars, the solution enables 360-degree omnidirectional perception of the surrounding environment and demonstrates real-time responsiveness to diverse weather conditions, lighting conditions, and edge-device scenarios. In addition, its advanced algorithms precisely detect and classify radar-captured obstacles and objects, and its usability and reliability have been proven through defense projects involving unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs).

In addition, DeepFusion AI plans to share development progress on the RAPA-RC (radar–camera) and RAPA-RL (radar–LiDAR) solutions, which are currently under development, with commercialization targeted for 2027, and to present the potential to expand its sensor-fusion technology across a wide range of industrial sectors.

A DeepFusion AI official said, “At CES, a global mega exhibition, we plan to introduce the core technologies and potential value of our sensor-fusion AI solutions that led to the top innovation award, and to seek new collaboration opportunities across more markets and industries.” The official added, “We are particularly looking forward to partnerships with automotive OEMs that are seeking reliable, high-efficiency detection technologies for the commercialization of autonomous driving.”

The official continued, “Among these efforts, we plan to explore entry into the European Union, where global companies and tier-one partners in autonomous driving and smart mobility are heavily concentrated and where demand for advanced technologies in the defense sector is also high,” and added, “At this CES, we aim to actively build networks to enable joint development and successful local proof-of-concept projects.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
